title: pvTemporalParticlesToPathlines
body:
## pvTemporalParticlesToPathlines

Builds trails from moving particles: it takes a point set whose points move between time steps (e.g. Lagrangian particles read from a solver, or a particle tracer's output) and joins each particle's successive positions into a polyline. ParaView loops over the input times itself up to the requested time. Output port 0 (Pathlines) holds the trails with TrailId and TrackLength; port 1 (Particles) holds one vertex at each trail's head. Particles are matched by IdChannelArray (global ids or point index by default). Use pvStreakLine to compute particle motion from a velocity field instead.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- By ParaView default only every 100th point is tracked (MaskPoints) and trails keep 25 steps; set MaskPoints to 1 and raise MaxTrackLength for complete paths.
- If particles are reordered between steps, matching by index scrambles the trails; set IdChannelArray to a persistent particle id.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `TemporalParticlesToPathlines`. Identity: `filters/ParticlePathLines`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: The input cells for which to create pathlines. Accepted data: explicit-point datasets (polygonal, unstructured or structured grids) (vtkPointSet). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkPointSet"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |
| `Selection` | Optional data input for the native Selection port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: Set a second input, which is a selection. Particles with the same Id in the selection as the primary input will be chosen for pathlines. Note that you must have the same IdChannelArray in the selection as the input. Accepted data: any dataset (meshes, grids, point sets) (vtkDataSet). | False | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataSet"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BackwardTime` | Compute particle path lines when time goes backward. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `IdChannelArray` | Specify the name of a scalar array which will be used to fetch the index of each point. This is necessary only if the particles change position (Id order) on each time step. The Id can be used to identify particles at each step and hence track them properly. If this array is set to "Global or Local IDs", the global point ids are used if they exist or the point index is otherwise. | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `KeepDeadTrails` | Keep the trails of particles that leave the domain. Use carefully as it may cause excessive memory consumption when generating many particle trails. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `MaskPoints` | Set the number of particles to track as a ratio of the input. Example: setting MaskPoints to 10 will track every 10th point. | `{"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `MaxStepDistance` | If a particle disappears from one end of a simulation and reappears on the other side, the track left will be unrepresentative. Set a MaxStepDistance{x,y,z} which acts as a threshold above which if a step occurs larger than the value (for the dimension), the track will be dropped and restarted after the step. That is, the part before the wrap around will be dropped and the newer part kept. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `MaxTrackLength` | If the particles being traced animate for a long time, the trails or traces will become long and stringy. Setting the MaxTraceTimeLength will limit how much of the trace is displayed. Tracks longer then the Max will disappear and the trace will appear like a snake of fixed length which progresses as the particle moves. This length is given with respect to timesteps. | `{"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |

  "id": "result",
